title: The believer in Pharaoh's house
hook: a man of Pharaoh's family who hid his faith speaks up for Musa (40:28)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Forgiver of sin, and your line was he accepts the return. Did you receive someone's turning back like a gift? Day five hundred sixty-two.

Pharaoh's court. The decision is nearly made. Pharaoh says: let me kill Musa, and let him call on his Lord. I'm afraid he'll change your religion, or spread corruption in the land. The advisers are nodding. It's the kind of room where disagreeing could cost you everything. And then a voice speaks up from inside the circle. Not an outsider, not one of Musa's people. A member of Pharaoh's own family. He has kept his faith hidden for who knows how long. Today, he can't keep quiet anymore.

Surah Ghafir, verse twenty-eight. Pickthall: "And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah". This is why some call the surah Al-Mu'min, the Believer. He's never named. Listen to how carefully he argues. He doesn't announce his faith. He asks a question. Would you kill a man just for saying my Lord is Allah? Then he reasons with them on their own terms. If he's lying, his lie is on him. If he's telling the truth, some of what he warns you about will reach you. You lose nothing by leaving him alone. He's not grandstanding. He's trying to save a life in a room that doesn't want to hear it. And he keeps going, over many verses. He reminds them of nations destroyed before them. He tells them about Yusuf, who came to Egypt long before and was doubted too. He calls them to salvation while they call him to the fire. And finally, verse forty-four, he says: you'll remember what I'm telling you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Verse forty-five: so Allah protected him from the evils they plotted. There's a moment in the Prophet's life that echoes this. Bukhari reports that when a man in Mecca seized the Prophet ﷺ and twisted his cloak around his neck, Abu Bakr pushed him away and said these same words: would you kill a man because he says my Lord is Allah? One voice, inside the room, can be enough to stop the room.
screen: `WOULD YOU KILL A MAN FOR THIS?`

segments.voice: The practice: speak up quietly for someone. Sit, and think of a room you're often in, a team, a family chat, a group of friends, where someone gets talked about unfairly. Picture yourself saying one calm sentence for them. Not a speech. A question, like his: is that really fair? Hear how it sounds. Then entrust the rest, to God if you pray, or simply let it go. The bell holds the time.
The believer in Pharaoh's house. An unnamed man of Pharaoh's family who hid his faith, and spoke up to save Musa's life. Today's word.
screen: `THE BELIEVER IN PHARAOH'S HOUSE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: one voice inside. Today, when a room turns against someone who isn't there, be the one calm question from inside it. Day five hundred sixty-two.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers often cite the believer of Pharaoh's family as an example of wise, courageous speech, and many recite his words 'I entrust my affair to Allah' (40:44) in times of fear.

fork.setup: you're a member of Pharaoh's family, secretly a believer. Pharaoh wants Musa dead. what do you do?
options: ask: would you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah?
fork.reveal: he spoke up with a careful question and reasoned with them, and later entrusted his affair to Allah, who protected him.

original.note: Arabic: a believing man, which gives the surah its other name, Al-Mu'min.

trapdoor: what you thought: a minor character in the Musa story.
what it means: an insider who hid his faith, then risked everything with one careful question to save a life.
what a scholar hears: 40:28–45 gives him a long speech; Bukhari 3678 has Abu Bakr repeat 40:28 while defending the Prophet; tafsir offers names for him, but the text leaves him anonymous.

sources.quoted: And a believing man of Pharaoh's family, who hid his faith, said: Would ye kill a man because he saith: My Lord is Allah

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3678 (Abu Bakr defends the Prophet with 40:28)

notes: Pickthall wording of 40:28 (first part) quoted from memory; please confirm.

Tafsir gives names for the believer (e.g. Sim'an, Habib); the script leaves him unnamed as the Qur'an does.
